changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For prospects replacing a homegrown billing system: "Billing shouldn't be a tax on your roadmap. Change prices, add trials and handle proration in minutes, not a quarter of engineering work."
changes.why: The champion rejected the revenue framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap'), while the demo landed in roadmap-speed terms ('a quarter of roadmap in five minutes') against a system where every pricing change takes a quarter.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance and CFO audiences: "Your number, not our study. We'll build your payback case with you from your own engineering hours, billing errors and failed-payment losses, ready to present to your CFO." Use the independent study as background only, not as the payback answer.
changes.why: The champion said he couldn't get the deal past the CFO 'without a number that's ours'. When he asked for payback, we sent the generic study deck, and the session to build their own number never happened.

changes.change: For homegrown-billing prospects, lead with the cost of standing still: "What is your current billing system costing you? A quarter of roadmap on every pricing change, a system only one person understood, and subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it." Pair it with M10 smart retries as the recovered-revenue line in the cost model.
changes.why: Finance treated the project as a 'nice to have' because 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded'. Yet the interview already contained the cost of inaction (a departed builder, quarter-long pricing changes, failed-card lapses) and we never added it up.

changes.change: Add a migration proof point for subscription-billing switchers: a reference customer who moved off a homegrown or legacy billing system in stages without re-collecting cards, available for a peer call, not just a migration doc.
changes.why: We had a migration doc, but the champion wanted to talk to someone who had done it, and the interview does not show that he ever got that conversation.
